most_likely_explanation: A real ~1.7-1.8 e/s periodic (4.8945 d, ~2 h) loss of light located within ~2-3 arcsec of KIC 11138423 in all four Kepler seasons, physically consistent with a 2.0-2.5 Earth-radius transit of this early-M dwarf (duration matches a/R* for R*=0.534 Rsun at b<0.5). Every testable alternative was excluded: the bright TPF host KIC 11138418 shows -8+-9 ppm (PSF) / -5+-4 ppm (SAP) at the ephemeris; no resolved Gaia neighbour can supply the lost light (required eclipse depths 17% to >100%, and the pixel deficit sits in the target's own pixel, not at any of them); no catalogued KOI/TCE/EB/TOI/PS object or SIMBAD entry at the position; no coherent ephemeris contaminant (the single period-coherent harmonic match, Kepler-20 f at 4P, 426 arcmin away, is a chance hit that would populate only every fourth event); no survey-wide period cluster at 4.894 d; no rotation alias; per-event depth scatter is red noise (random-ephemeris calibration), no gap/quality-flag association, stable linear ephemeris over 4 years. One important finding is not a kill but must enter the evidence pack: the KBONUS fractional depth depends on season (900+-105 ppm in S0 vs 1698+-180 ppm in S3, 3.8 sigma; per-quarter chi2 38.6/16 vs random-ephemeris max 26.5) because the un-rescaled per-quarter PSF flux of the star varies from 1017 to 1789 e/s with the stamp geometry (season-dependent contamination by the host's PRF wings); the absolute dip is constant (raw-PSF 1.73 e/s, chi2 14.4/16; SAP 1.58 e/s, chi2 15.1/16; pixel-level 1.80 e/s), which is the behaviour of a source whose light is fully inside the photometry in every season. Remaining, untested alternatives are the standard ones for statistical validation: a sub-pixel (<2-3 arcsec) blended EB, a twin EB at 2P (odd/even agree to 0.35 sigma), or an on-target grazing low-mass companion (secondary < 27% of primary at 3 sigma).
surviving_strengths: Bright TPF host KIC 11138418 directly excluded: -8.1+-8.9 ppm (PSF) and -5.0+-3.7 ppm (SAP) at the ephemeris in its own KBONUS light curve; its total missing light (<2.4 e/s at 2 sigma) with a 0.1-0.2% per-pixel wing at the target's distance cannot supply the 1.7-1.9 e/s lost in the target's photometry

Independent season-stacked pixel analysis (18 TPFs, empirical host-PRF template): target pixel is the strongest deficit pixel in all four seasons (SNR 7.7, 7.4, 4.8, 5.7); PRF at target beats null by delta chi2 48/43/27/21 and beats PRF at host by 41/34/25/12; best-fit positions 1.7-2.9 arcsec from the Gaia position in different sky directions each season (mean offset +0.3, +1.1 arcsec); moving the source beyond the stamp edge is disfavoured in the three clean seasons (delta chi2 +4 to +33 per 0.5-1 px)

Absolute light lost per transit is constant across four CCD channels/orientations in raw PSF (1.73 e/s, chi2 14.4/16), raw SAP (1.58 e/s, chi2 15.1/16), PSF_FLUX_NOVA and the pixel-level fit (1.80 e/s): a leaking neighbour would vary with geometry
No resolved Gaia (G<20) neighbour can be the source: needed eclipse depths >=150% for all G>18.5 sources, 17-41% for the G=16.79 star 17 arcsec away whose position shows no deficit

Not known anywhere: no KOI/TCE/Kepler-EB/PS within 5 arcmin, no TOI/PS in a 3 arcmin box (Exoplanet Archive TAP 2026-10-17), SIMBAD has nothing at the position, not among Bienias & Szabo 2025's seven candidates nor the Kepler Bonus team's public BOI-1.01

No coherent ephemeris contaminant: 203 KOI/TCE/EB harmonic matches within 0.2%, only Kepler-20 f (4P, 98 ppm, 426 arcmin, different module) is period-coherent and phase-aligned, which cannot populate every epoch; only this star in 6,365 has a real detection near 4.894 d

Light-curve statistics clean: odd/even 0.35 sigma; secondary +51+-106 ppm at phase 0.5 (<27% of primary at 3 sigma), no dip at any other phase (181-trial scan); LS power at P negligible (amp ~100 ppm, systematics at 40 d only); per-event chi2/dof 1.38 at the 73rd percentile of random ephemerides on the same light curve; near-gap events 1114+-215 vs others 1239+-67 ppm; per-year t0 shifts within +-7 min; flagged-cadence fraction in transit 7.6% vs 8.0% overall; PSF-fit red chi2 unchanged in transit

Duration/density consistent: T14 1.76-2.04 h measured vs 1.95-2.07 h for a central transit of a 0.50-0.60 Msun, 0.534 Rsun dwarf (a/R* 18-19); Gaia M_G 7.60 at BP-RP 1.72 is main sequence; RUWE 1.06; inverted-flux null SDE 8.2 vs 31.3 (re-derivation)
checks_run: Known-object search: KOI, DR25 TCE, Kepler EB (Kirk+2016), confirmed planets within 5 arcmin from data/known (fetched 2026-10-17); TOI and PS tables via Exoplanet Archive TAP in a 3 arcmin box; SIMBAD within 30 arcsec and 3 arcmin with object types; Bienias & Szabo 2025 candidate list; Kepler Bonus team public candidate

Ephemeris/harmonic match (P, P/2, 2P, P/3, 3P, 2P/3, 3P/2, P/4, 4P; |dP/P|<2e-3) against all KOIs, TCEs and Kepler EBs field-wide with phase alignment and period coherence over 300 epochs (redteam/ephemeris_match.py)
Survey-wide check of triage_all.csv (6,365 stars, real and inverted) for detections near 4.894 d or its harmonics
KBONUS light curve of the TPF host KIC 11138418 downloaded and folded at the ephemeris in PSF, SAP and PSF_FLAT flux (random-phase box errors)
KBONUS source catalogue: all sources on TPF 11138418 and within 40 arcsec; MAST download attempts for the six Gaia neighbours (none exist in KBONUS)
Required eclipse depth for each Gaia neighbour from the measured host-PRF wing fraction per pixel

Per-quarter and per-season box depths in stitched FLUX, SAP_FLUX, PSF_FLAT_FLUX and per-quarter PSF_FLUX_NOVA; depth-vs-PSFFRAC regression; random-ephemeris calibration of the per-quarter chi2 (60 trials); absolute e/s dips from the un-rescaled per-quarter extension fluxes (redteam/lc_checks.py, season_table, raw_quarter_flux)
Per-event depths with local-noise errors, chi2 vs constant and its calibration with 150 random ephemerides; strongest-event fraction; gap-proximity split; per-year t0 scan for TTV/period drift
Quality-flag fraction in transit vs overall and bits present; PSF-fit RED_CHI2 in vs out of transit; SAP_BKG (NaN in product)
Phase scan of a 1.95 h box over 181 phases, secondary at 0.5 with 1x and 3x duration, odd/even with pipeline parity
Lomb-Scargle 0.25-60 d on raw per-quarter-normalised flux; power at P and P/2

Season-stacked per-pixel event-differenced deficit maps from the 18 cached TPFs with an empirical PRF template (shifted out-of-transit image): chi2 at target, at host, along the host-to-target line beyond the stamp edge, grid search for best position with amplitude errors, conversion of best positions to sky offsets per season (redteam/pixel_checks.py, sky_offsets)
Duration/density/radius consistency for M*=0.50-0.60 Msun, R*=0.534 Rsun; Gaia CMD and RUWE sanity
Re-read of vet.json, events.csv, fold_events.png, pixel.json/diffimages.png (v1, v15, v16) and the independent re-derivation results.json
what_would_settle_it: Adopt a depth definition that is immune to the season-dependent KBONUS contamination: absolute lost light (1.7-1.8 e/s) divided by an independent flux estimate for the star (Gaia G with the host-derived zero point ~1450 e/s, or a full-scene PRF re-extraction), and report Rp as 2.0-2.5 Re with a per-season depth table in the evidence pack
TRICERATOPS run using the pixel-level ~2-3 arcsec exclusion radius and the Gaia G<20 neighbour list, reporting FPP and NFPP
Speckle or AO imaging of KIC 11138423 (G=17.35) to bound stellar companions at 0.1-2 arcsec

A ground-based or short-cadence transit observation (1.2-1.8 ppt, 2 h) to resolve ingress/egress and test the twin-EB (2P) and grazing-companion alternatives; radial velocities are impractical at this magnitude
Re-extraction of the star's photometry with the host PRF fully modelled, to confirm the absolute-e/s constancy and remove the season dependence
